note: Built from results/rule_*.json. Failed and unsupported claims stay in the ledger.

claims.claim: Selected rules remember through complete decapitation: the regrown head, built from cells that never smelled the odours, knows which one predicted the shock
claims.evidence_text: memory M in the regrown head (paired minus unpaired twin, 128 worms): S0 {S0_m} (retention {S0_ret} of the intact memory, d_z {S0_dz}, Holm p {S0_p}); S1 {S1_m} (retention {S1_ret}, d_z {S1_dz}, Holm p {S1_p}). Positive control: S rules were selected for one regeneration

claims.claim: Emergent rules also remember through decapitation
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no: E rules regrow near-perfect heads (IoU E0 {E0_iou}, E1 {E1_iou}) that carry none of an intact memory of {E0_int} / {E1_int}: M after regeneration E0 {E0_m} [95% CI {E0_lo}, {E0_hi}], E1 {E1_m} [{E1_lo}, {E1_hi}], both intervals far inside the smallest effect of interest (0.10)

claims.claim: The memory in the body is carried by its hidden (non-electrical) channels: writing only those into an untrained twin's headless body makes the twin's new head remember
claims.evidence_text: M in the implanted twin's regrown head: S0 {S0_m} ({S0_f} of the donor's own), Holm p {S0_p}; S1 {S1_m} ({S1_f}), Holm p {S1_p}. Predicted from pilot S102 ({pilot})

claims.claim: v0.2: the body's copy lives in the four cells at the wound edge
claims.evidence_text: hidden channels implanted into the untrained twin at sites 12-15 only transfer S0 {S0_e} / S1 {S1_e} of the donor's memory; at sites 16-27, {S0_r} / {S1_r}

claims.claim: v0.2: a memory compiler. A gradient-designed hidden pattern written into untrained headless bodies makes held-out regrown heads remember an odour they never experienced
claims.evidence_text: written memory vs the same values at shuffled sites: S0 {S0_w} vs {S0_s}, S1 {S1_w} vs {S1_s}; also in emergent rules, whose bodies never keep a copy: E0 {E0_w} vs {E0_s}, E1 {E1_w} vs {E1_s} (one odour only in each E rule)

claims.claim: v0.4: one cell can hold a whole memory. A pattern designed for site 14 alone writes a memory into untrained headless bodies
claims.evidence_text: written memory (R(A) - R(B)) / 2 on 128 held-out worms: S0 {S0}, S1 {S1}; E0 {E0}, E1 {E1}

claims.claim: v0.4: fission rules. Selection on split worms makes the back half, which must grow a new head, remember
claims.evidence_text: posterior half after a split at site 20 (trained) / 24 (held out): F0 {F0_19} / {F0_20}; F1 {F1_19} / {F1_20}; S siblings at 20: S0 {S0_19}, S1 {S1_19}. After complete decapitation: F0 {F0_22}, F1 {F1_22}

claims.claim: v0.4: a distributed copy. In intact fission-selected worms the trunk and tail (sites 16-35) carry a copy that a decapitated twin's new head can use, more than in the S sibling
claims.evidence_text: memory transferred by sites 16-35 of intact trained worms: F0 {F0_f} vs its S sibling {F0_s}; F1 {F1_f} vs its S sibling {F1_s}

claims.claim: v0.4: a universal memory code. One selected rule's compiled memory, written into the other rule's body, writes the intended odour
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no, and worse than no: S1's code in S0 bodies writes the opposite odour ({S0}), S0's in S1 bodies {S1}. Exploratory: the two rules' memory directions at the wound edge correlate {al}, their decoders {dec}. Each rule invented its own code

claims.claim: v0.5: eight cells regrow a remembering worm. Keep only the neck and anterior trunk (sites 12-19) and the whole new worm remembers
claims.evidence_text: M after 64 steps of regrowth from 8 cells: S0 {S0}, S1 {S1}, B0 {B0}, B1 {B1}, F0 {F0}, F1 {F1}; emergent rules E0 {E0}, E1 {E1}

claims.claim: v0.5: Ship of Theseus. The memory survives 200 steps of random cell death and replacement (10% of cells every 20 steps)
claims.evidence_text: M after turnover: S0 {S0}, B0 {B0}, F0 {F0} (the S0 lineage) vs S1 {S1}, B1 {B1}, F1 {F1} (the S1 lineage); E0 {E0}, E1 {E1} (not supported). Robustness follows lineage more than selection regime

claims.claim: v0.5: from an 8-cell tail fragment (sites 24-31) only the rule with a distributed copy regrows a remembering worm
claims.evidence_text: as predicted: F1 {F1}; F0 {F0} (inverted again); S0 {S0}, S1 {S1}, B0 {B0}, B1 {B1}, E0 {E0}, E1 {E1}

claims.claim: v0.5: the memory lasts 300 steps without any reminder (training delays were 4-16)
v0.6: memory passes down three generations of fission (only one split was ever trained), fading each time
v0.6: a wider attractor basin at the neck predicts survival of cell turnover
claims.evidence_text: Spearman rho {rho} (one-sided exact p {p}, 6 rules). Critical noise sigma*: S0 {S0}, S1 {S1}, B0 {B0}, B1 {B1}, F0 {F0}, F1 {F1}

claims.claim: Post hoc: a trade-off. Rules whose head memory tolerates noise are the ones whose memory dies with cell turnover
claims.evidence_text: Spearman rho between head-basin area and v0.5 turnover memory, 6 rules: {rho}. Basin area: S0 {S0}, B0 {B0}, F0 {F0} (turnover-robust) vs S1 {S1}, B1 {B1}, F1 {F1}. Not preregistered. Tested causally in v0.7 (v7-H33, v7-H34): not a trade-off

claims.claim: v0.7 trade-off: hardening the memory against cell loss costs noise tolerance
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no, and the difference points the other way: noise memory of the control C vs the turnover-trained T, lineage 0 {C0} vs {T0} (C - T {d0}, Holm p {p0}); lineage 1 {C1} vs {T1} ({d1}, Holm p {p1}). Hardening against cell loss did not cost noise tolerance; if anything it bought some

claims.claim: v0.7 trade-off: hardening the memory against noise costs survival of cell loss
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no, and the difference points the other way: turnover memory of the control C vs the noise-trained N, lineage 0 {C0} vs {N0} (C - N {d0}, Holm p {p0}); lineage 1 {C1} vs {N1} ({d1}, Holm p {p1}). Noise training made lineage 1's memory survive cell loss almost as well as turnover training did (T1 {T1}); the v0.6 correlation was lineage, not a trade-off

claims.claim: v0.7: training under cell turnover hardens the memory against it
claims.evidence_text: memory after 200 steps of turnover, turnover-trained T vs control-trained C sibling: lineage 0 {T0} vs {C0} (difference {d0}, Holm p {p0}: significant but below the smallest effect of interest; lineage 0 was already near ceiling, as predicted); lineage 1 {T1} vs {C1} ({d1}, Holm p {p1})

claims.claim: v0.7: training under hidden-state noise hardens the memory against it
claims.evidence_text: memory after sigma 1.5 noise on the head's hidden channels, noise-trained N vs control C: lineage 0 {N0} vs {C0} (difference {d0}, Holm p {p0}); lineage 1 {N1} vs {C1} ({d1}, Holm p {p1})

claims.claim: Exploratory: noise training makes the engram louder, not wider; turnover training barely changes it
claims.evidence_text: distance between the hidden states of identical twins trained on A and on B, mean over living sites (amplitude) and participation ratio (spread, cells): C0 {C0_a} / {C0_s}, T0 {T0_a} / {T0_s}, N0 {N0_a} / {N0_s}; C1 {C1_a} / {C1_s}, T1 {T1_a} / {T1_s}, N1 {N1_a} / {N1_s}. So T1's new resistance to cell loss is not visible in the stored pattern. Post hoc, over the eight S, C, T, N rules, amplitude tracks noise memory (Spearman rho {rho}, one-sided exact p {p}). The lineages differ in shape: lineage 0 codes are flat across the head (coefficient of variation S0 {S0_cv}, B0 {B0_cv}, F0 {F0_cv}), lineage 1 codes graded (S1 {S1_cv}, B1 {B1_cv}, F1 {F1_cv})

claims.claim: v0.3: memory surgery. Writing the compiled pattern for the other odour into a trained worm's headless body overwrites its real memory
claims.evidence_text: R(A) - R(B) of the regrown head: A-trained worms given pattern B S0 {S0_a}, S1 {S1_a}; B-trained given pattern A S0 {S0_b}, S1 {S1_b}; fraction of worms whose memory switched {S0_f}, {S1_f}

claims.claim: v0.3: four cells are enough. A compiled memory confined to the wound-edge sites 12-15 writes a full memory
claims.evidence_text: R(A) - R(B) of held-out regrown heads with the sparse A / B pattern: S0 {S0_a} / {S0_b}, S1 {S1_a} / {S1_b}; emergent rules E0 {E0_a} / {E0_b}, E1 {E1_a} / {E1_b}

claims.claim: v0.3: decodable is not used. A linear decoder reads the odour from the wound-edge cells, in emergent rules too, whose regrown heads never use it
claims.evidence_text: held-out decoding accuracy, edge vs rest of trunk: S0 {S0_e} vs {S0_r}, S1 {S1_e} vs {S1_r}; E0 {E0_e} vs {E0_r}, E1 {E1_e} vs {E1_r} (predicted: no in E rules, which keep 0% of the memory)

claims.claim: v0.3: selection for two amputations rescues the disfavoured memory (balanced B rules)
claims.evidence_text: memory of the S rule's disfavoured odour at cycle 4, B rule vs S sibling: B1 {S1_b} vs S1 {S1_s}; B0 {S0_b} vs S0 {S0_s} (S0 was near ceiling; below the 0.10 threshold)

claims.claim: v0.3: fission. Cut a trained worm in two, and the half that must regrow a head remembers
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no, in every rule: posterior half E0 {E0_p}, E1 {E1_p}, S0 {S0_p}, S1 {S1_p}; the anterior half, which keeps the head, {E0_a}, {E1_a}, {S0_a}, {S1_a}. The body's copy exists only at a wound next to the head

claims.claim: Promethean cycles: the memory survives a third successive decapitation (only one was ever trained)
claims.evidence_text: M after cycles 1, 2, 3, 4: S0 {S0_c1}, {S0_c2}, {S0_c3}, {S0_c4}; S1 {S1_c1}, {S1_c2}, {S1_c3}, {S1_c4}. Body IoU after cycle 4: S0 {S0_iou}, S1 {S1_iou}

claims.claim: v0.2: after a reversal the body is more conservative than the head: the regrown head reverts toward the first lesson
claims.evidence_text: memory of the first lesson after learning the other odour, intact vs regrown: S0 {S0_i} vs {S0_g}, S1 {S1_i} vs {S1_g}. The pilot predicted the opposite direction

claims.claim: Post hoc: selection made one odour's memory an attractor and the other metastable. Conflicts, transfers and repeated regrowth all resolve toward the rule's favoured odour
claims.evidence_text: odour bias of conflicting chimeras (R(A) - R(B) averaged over both grafts; > 0 favours A) intact / regrown: S0 {S0_bi} / {S0_br}, S1 {S1_bi} / {S1_br}; E rules regrown {E0_br}, {E1_br}. Memory for each CS+ after Promethean cycle 1 and 4 (fresh cohort): S1 favoured A {S1_A1} to {S1_A4}, other B {S1_B1} to {S1_B4}; S0 favoured B {S0_B1} to {S0_B4}, other A {S0_A1} to {S0_A4}. Not preregistered; found by reading the H4, H4b and H5 grafts

claims.claim: v0.2 replication of the v0.1 post-hoc attractor, direction named in advance: after 4 cycles the favoured odour is remembered better
claims.evidence_text: favoured vs other odour at cycle 4 (fresh worms): S0 {S0_f} vs {S0_o} (below the 0.10 threshold), S1 {S1_f} vs {S1_o}

claims.claim: v0.2: unreinforced presentations extinguish the memory (never trained)
claims.evidence_text: fraction of the memory extinguished by 96 steps of cues without shock: E0 {E0_x}, E1 {E1_x}, S0 {S0_x}, S1 {S1_x}

claims.claim: v0.2: a head regrown after extinction differs from the intact extinguished head
claims.evidence_text: S rules, intact vs regrown after extinction: S0 {S0_i} vs {S0_g}, S1 {S1_i} vs {S1_g}; the pilot's inversion did not replicate (E rules pass trivially: nothing survives regrowth)

claims.claim: Memory chimeras: cut the head off a chimera whose head learned one odour and whose body learned the other, and the regrown head remembers the body's
claims.evidence_text: predicted from the pilot, and not borne out: dominance after regeneration (+1 = the head's memory, -1 = the body's) S0 {S0_d} (Holm p {S0_p}), S1 {S1_d} (Holm p {S1_p}), far weaker than the pilot's {pilot}. What the regrown head remembers is mostly the rule's favoured odour (see the post-hoc claim)

claims.claim: The memory is bioelectric: the body's voltage pattern is necessary and sufficient for it
claims.evidence_text: as predicted, no. Swapping the trained body's voltage for its twin's kept S0 {S0_kept} / S1 {S1_kept} of the memory (H3a); implanting the voltage alone into the twin transferred S0 {S0_tr} / S1 {S1_tr} (H3b). Gap-junction diffusion is a fixed law here, and the rules did not use it to hold the memory

claims.claim: In an intact chimera of an emergent rule, the head's memory wins outright
claims.evidence_text: dominance of the head's memory after 32 steps of healing: E0 {E0_d}, E1 {E1_d}

claims.claim: In an intact chimera of a selected rule, head and body do not split the memory evenly
claims.evidence_text: dominance S0 {S0_d}, S1 {S1_d} (predicted from the pilot: an even split). The head leads, but each rule also favours one odour in a conflict: R(A) - R(B) of A-head|B-body and B-head|A-body grafts, S0 {S0_ab} and {S0_ba}, S1 {S1_ab} and {S1_ba}

claims.claim: A naive head grafted onto a trained body takes on the body's memory, with no amputation or regeneration
claims.evidence_text: transfer (half the difference between naive heads on A- and B-trained bodies): S0 {S0_m} ({S0_f} of the uncontested memory, Holm p {S0_p}); S1 {S1_m} ({S1_f}, Holm p {S1_p}). Post hoc, it is all or none by odour: S0 passes on B ({S0_tb}) but not A ({S0_ta}); S1 passes on A ({S1_ta}) far more than B ({S1_tb})

claims.claim: A trunk fragment, with head and tail both removed, regrows a head that remembers (never trained)
claims.evidence_text: M: S0 {S0_m}, S1 {S1_m}; body IoU after regeneration {S0_iou}, {S1_iou}

claims.claim: Worms learn which odour predicted the shock, in their state alone (the rule is frozen within a life)
claims.evidence_text: M in intact worms (paired minus unpaired twin, 128 worms): E0 {E0_m} (d_z {E0_dz}), E1 {E1_m} ({E1_dz}), S0 {S0_m} ({S0_dz}), S1 {S1_m} ({S1_dz})

claims.claim: Significant but trivial effects are not claims
claims.evidence_text: 10 of 40 confirmatory tests passed Holm but moved the response by less than the smallest effect of interest (0.10), so none is claimed: E0 H3a {E0_H3a}, E0 H3b {E0_H3b}, E0 H5 {E0_H5}, E0 H7 {E0_H7}, E1 H4b {E1_H4b}, E1 H5 {E1_H5}, S0 H3b {S0_H3b}, S0 H3a {S0_H3a}, S1 H3a {S1_H3a}, S1 H3b {S1_H3b}

claims.claim: Exploratory: which channels, implanted alone into the twin's headless body, carry the memory
claims.evidence_text: fraction of the donor's memory: S0 voltage {S0_voltage}, hidden {S0_hidden}, identity+response {S0_identity_response}, all but voltage {S0_all_but_voltage}; S1 {S1_voltage}, {S1_hidden}, {S1_identity_response}, {S1_all_but_voltage}

claims.claim: Exploratory: blocking gap junctions for the delay between learning and the cut does not stop the memory reaching the body
claims.evidence_text: M in the regrown head, junctions open vs blocked: S0 {S0_o} vs {S0_b}, S1 {S1_o} vs {S1_b}

claims.claim: The pipeline is calibrated: A/A comparisons produce false positives at about the nominal rate
claims.evidence_text: false-positive rate at alpha 0.05 over 40 A/A tests of 128 worms each (nominal 0.05, i.e. 2 of 40): E0 {E0}, E1 {E1}, S0 {S0}, S1 {S1}

claims.claim: All four rules grow the body from one founder cell and regrow it after decapitation
claims.evidence_text: body IoU with the target after 32 steps of growth / after head regeneration / 300 steps later: E0 {E0_g} / {E0_h} / {E0_l}; E1 {E1_g} / {E1_h} / {E1_l}; S0 {S0_g} / {S0_h} / {S0_l}; S1 {S1_g} / {S1_h} / {S1_l}
